## Thesis

::: {#refs}
:::

**Bachelor's thesis · Heidelberg University · CERN-THESIS-2024-042**

The bachelor thesis develops a neural-network-based track-matching algorithm
for recovering electron tracks in LHCb's real-time analysis trigger. The method
achieves electron tracking efficiencies above 90% while keeping the fake-track
fraction below 15%.

[View the CERN record](https://repository.cern/records/tsgg5-mnd54){.btn .btn-primary}
[Download the thesis](https://repository.cern/records/tsgg5-mnd54/files/CERN-THESIS-2024-042.pdf?download=1){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

## Seminar work

### The Physics of Nuclear Spin Systems

Seminar: *Methods of Physics in Biology and Medicine*, Heidelberg University,
17 December 2024. The report introduces nuclear spin systems and develops the
physical principles underlying nuclear magnetic resonance imaging; the slide
deck presents the accompanying seminar talk.
